title: EdenPay partnership outreach — personal slate
content:
Quick thesis / purpose:
- Short personal scratch for EdenPay (mid-size payments processor, EU+US). Doing early account research + 1st outbound drafts, objection handling, and a simple pilot proposal. Keep this light — shareable with Solutions if we get interest.

Account snapshot (public + notes):
- HQ: Berlin, HQ dev org ~70 engs.
- Recent funding: Series B (2024).
- Product: payments processing for marketplaces, recurring billing, fraud/risk engine, embeddable widgets.
- Compliance: PCI-DSS scope, storing tokens in their vault, strong security posture.
- Signals: job posts for ML infra / real-time scoring roles; blog post about reducing latency for anti-fraud checks (Jan 2026).
- Likely priorities: reduce fraud false positives, lower decision latency, cut costs on inference for risk models.

Org map (to validate):
- CTO / Head of Platform: Lukas Berger (likely decision owner for infra choices).
- Head of Risk / Fraud: Anna Petrov — buyer for model infra + evals.
- Engineering manager(s) for real-time: two teams, one for payments pipeline, one for risk scoring microservices.
- Security/compliance: DPO or Security lead (needs signatures for private deployments).

Technical signals / stack hints:
- References to Kafka + Flink in job postings.
- Using PyTorch for their model teams (mentions on careers page).
- AWS heavy: EKS, S3; some self-hosted Redis for caching.
- PCI scope suggests Private deployment will be compelling.

Pain & value hypothesis (how Redwood helps):
- Problem A: 50–200ms tail latency for fraud scoring is causing checkout friction and higher bot rejection — they call out latency-sensitive scoring in blog.
  Redwood value: dedicated low-latency inference (pinned capacity + small-seq optimizations), fallback model variants to maintain service during spikes.
- Problem B: High per-request cost for scoring many models (ensemble) at scale.
  Redwood value: batching, KV prefix caching for repeated contexts, quantization & optimized kernels to cut unit cost by 2–4x.
- Problem C: Compliance / auditability for model decisions.
  Redwood value: private deployment with audit logs, KMS integration, and deterministic rollouts + eval hooks.

Measure of success (what we can promise/ask for pilot):
- Latency: reduce P95 scoring latency by 30–50% for a selected endpoint.
- Cost: target 30% reduction in per-decision inference cost via batching/quantization.
- Reliability: maintain >99.9% availability for the scoring endpoint under baseline traffic.

Pilot proposal (lightweight):
- Scope: 2-week PoC integrating their risk model(s) into Redwood Private/Dedicated dev pool, run parallel to prod traffic (shadow) for 2 weeks.
- Deliverables: latency report (P50/P95), per-token cost analysis, quality parity check (A/B on sample traffic), short runbook for rollout.
- Ask: sandbox creds, a small sample of anonymized scoring payloads, access to one risk model container or model artifact, SLA contact for ops.

Outbound emails (A/B drafts)
- Short cold (subject options): "Cut fraud decision latency at checkout — quick idea"
Draft A (short):
Hi Anna —
I read your post about checkout latency and wanted to share a quick idea: we helped a marketplace reduce fraud-scoring P95 by ~40% while halving inference cost using a combined dedicated + batching approach.
Would you be open to a 20-min call next week to see if the same approach maps to EdenPay?
— Maya

Draft B (context + pilot ask):
Hi Anna,
I’m Maya on the Redwood Inference partnerships team. We specialize in serving latency-sensitive risk models (dedicated capacity + private deployment for PCI workloads).
From what I can see, EdenPay runs a PyTorch-based scoring pipeline and has strict PCI constraints — we’ve run short pilots where teams could shadow traffic for 2 weeks and get actionable P95/cost numbers. If this is interesting I can share a one-page pilot plan and a short list of data needed.
Availability Thu/Fri?
Thanks,
Maya

Cold call / intro script (30–60s):
- Intro: "Hi Anna, Maya from Redwood — we work with payments teams to shave inference latency and cost for fraud/risk models."
- Value: quick stat — "in pilots we’ve cut P95 by ~40% and inference spend by ~30%"
- Ask: "Would you be open to a short call to share our pilot plan and see if this maps to EdenPay?"

Objection handling (anticipated):
- "We run everything on AWS / EC2 / EKS": Redwood Dedicated or Private can integrate with VPC and support EKS-adjacent workflows; we can do a shadow pilot with minimal infra changes.
- "PCI compliance concerns": we offer Private deployments with customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and an on-prem option if needed. Share SOC-type artifacts and security questionnaire early.
- "We don’t want vendor lock-in / maintain another runtime": emphasize same API abstraction, ability to pin model versions, and migration patterns (exportable model artifacts + fallback to existing infra). Show MLOps-friendly hooks and eval comparisons.
- "Cost-savings unclear": offer to run a short cost model using their sample request profile and baseline token counts; propose a guarantee-ish measurable target in pilot.

Open questions / things to validate quickly:
- Confirm model formats (PyTorch state_dict? Torchscript? ONNX?).
- Typical token/sequence lengths for scoring requests (we need distribution to size GPU pools).
- Current P95/P50 numbers for risk endpoint + traffic patterns (burstiness).
- Compliance gate: who signs for private deployment + what docs they need (ISO/SOC/PCI artifacts).

Next steps (if Anna interested):
- Day 0–2: NDA / Security questionnaire -> confirm ability to run shadow traffic.
- Day 3–7: quick ingest + small smoke test (1 node).
- Week 2: run shadowing, collect latency/cost/quality metrics, 1 interim sync.
- Week 3: present report, propose rollout.

Quick operational notes (for Solutions):
- If they ask for low-effort path: show Dedicated with reserved pool + canary fallback to open-model cheaper variants.
- For compliance: prepare short packet (SOC2 summary, PCI scope notes, KMS diagrams).
- For cost modeling: ask for 7-day sample of scoring traces and model sizes.

Personal TODOs (short):
- Validate Anna Petrov contact on LinkedIn (done) -> grab email.
- Draft short pilot 1-pager (1 page) and security packet template (fill placeholders).
- Request sample scoring payloads + baseline P95 numbers in the first meeting.

Notes to self / channel snippets to use:
- "40% P95 reduction" and "~30% per-decision cost" are good heuristics, but graft to actual pilot numbers quickly.
- Bring up shadow mode as the low-friction step.
- If security pushes back, escalate to Solutions Eng for an early technical sync.

Unresolved / guard rails:
- Don’t promise exact % savings; couch as estimates and tie to pilot metrics.
- Keep pilot low-effort; goal is actionable metrics, not full migration.

End of slate.
